`REVISE` with **1 Blocking, 1 Important and no Optional** findings — the
same shape as rounds 40 and 41, and the **fifth consecutive round to find
nothing in the design**: its architecture section records that the mechanism
was deliberately not re-audited, that `materialise()`, `pin()`, the `-P -B`
re-exec, the runtime-root ladder, the refusal taxonomy, the exit-code
contract and the CLI surface are unchanged in the text it read, and that
CP4B's admissibility model, clause table and fixtures stand as rounds 39, 40
and 41 verified them. It answered all three things revision 42 asked of it by
running rather than reading: it re-derived the corrected population from the
disposition sections instead of from this document's own sentence, ran the
partition pin's new clause (v) against its declared failing instantiation,
and ran the component pin over all three of its declared regions. It
reproduced every figure this document published save one.

**Both findings are accepted in full; neither is rejected, deferred or
narrowed**, and each premise was reproduced against this repository before
its row was written. The Blocking finding sits one layer under the repair
round 41 bought. Clause (d) of the component pin — *the sequence equals what
the command-line half's own extraction answers over the published text* — is
the clause that makes the other three a pin rather than an
internal-consistency check, and it is only ever as decidable as the
extraction it invokes. That extraction had **three** unstated conventions,
and one of them decides a published figure.

**The class it lands in is this document's other named failure shape.** The
reading an implementer gets by default is a markdown library's own code-span
content, and CommonMark removes a span's padding only when the span carries
both a leading and a trailing space. This half's own first prefix quotation
carries only a trailing one, so read that way it begins with the prefix:
clause (i) admits it, clause (ii) removes it, the strict total is nine rather
than eight, and the pin's clause (c) then needs a loose total of twenty-five
where the extraction answers twenty-four. Clauses (c) and (d) both go red
**against a correct, unmodified document** — the shape `OPUS-R33-B1`,
`OPUS-R34-B2`, `OPUS-R35-B1`, `OPUS-R36-B1` and `OPUS-R37-B1` share, and the
one grading on the size of the edit would have missed.

| Finding | Disposition (each premise reproduced against this repository before the row was written) |
|---|---|
| **`OPUS-R42-B1`** (Blocking) — the command-line half's extraction has an unstated normalisation step; under the CommonMark reading of a code span the strict total is nine rather than the published eight, and two of the component pin's four clauses go red against a correct document | **Accepted in full, and both readings were reproduced before this row was written.** Extraction over revision 42's published text: with each span's content stripped, clause (i) admits **8** and clause (ii) drops none; with CommonMark content, this row's own first prefix quotation — which ends in a space and begins with none, so the padding rule does not reach it — is admitted by clause (i) and removed by clause (ii), giving **9** and **1**. The loose total is **24** under both readings, so clause (c) would need **25**, and clause (d) compares **9** against a published **8**: two clauses red with nothing wrong in the document. The survivor count is **7** under all four combinations of the two ambiguities, which is why no figure this half itself asserts moved and why only the pin could see it. **The first of the finding's two remedies is taken** — declare the strip rather than restate the figures — for the reason the finding gives: it is what the run behind revision 42's bundle already did, and it makes this row's own prefix quotation a loose-only admission **by rule** rather than by accident. **The declaration is a clause of the recogniser row rather than prose elsewhere**, and it covers all three conventions this recogniser has needed rather than only the one that moved a figure: paragraph-scoped backtick pairing, whitespace-normalised text so a wrapped span is one span and not two, and the span's text with leading and trailing whitespace removed — with a clause saying *why* the strip is load-bearing, so a later editor does not delete it as noise. Round 41 recorded the first two in passing and conditioned them on the row being next edited; revision 42 edited that row and did not add them, which is why they are stated now rather than left conditional a second time. **The trailing space's *"one ambiguity"* claim is corrected in the same revision**: it is one of the ambiguities the row declares, and the paragraph now records the span-text convention run both ways over the published text exactly as it already records the space run both ways — the answer does not move for the half, it does move for the pin, and both are stated |
| **`OPUS-R42-I1`** (Important) — the bundle's `REVIEW_REQUEST.md` carried revision 41's challenge section into a revision-42 bundle, and one figure it publishes is false of the plan it ships with | **Accepted in full**, and confirmed line by line against the bundle rather than from the finding: the file's header block and its account of what changed were rewritten for revision 42 while its closing section was revision 41's text unchanged. The disagreements are not stray phrases — round 40 named where round 41 belongs, four pin clauses where the revision's headline repair is the fifth, round 41 missing from the list of rounds that covered the design, and a *claimed answer* of `forty` against `plan_revision` 41 − 1 where the document in the same bundle states `forty-one` at all three occurrences. The last is what makes this more than tidiness: it is a figure the reviewer is invited to reproduce, and the same file's own instruction is to grade a non-reproducing figure as this defect class's next appearance. **No repository instrument can see it** — `.ai-review/` is gitignored, which `OPUS-R40-B1` settled — so the repair is the shape the registry re-embed already has rather than a new test: the section is rewritten for this round, the plan's change list no longer claims the author-written bundle files were regenerated **without a check that they were**, and `TEST_RESULTS.md` **§0g** compares each of the two against the revision and HEAD it ships with, beside §0f's byte comparison of the registry table. The finding's grading is accepted too: Important rather than Blocking, because nothing in the plan, the registry or the mapping is wrong and no half or pin is affected — but it must not go to the manual external stage as it stands, since that bundle is what a human hands to the external reviewer |

## Plan review round 43 — disposition

Round 43 reviewed bundle `b17b8c20…` at plan revision 43 and returned
`REVISE` with **1 Blocking, 1 Important and no Optional** findings — the
same shape as rounds 40, 41 and 42, and the **sixth consecutive round to
find nothing in the design**: its architecture section records that
`materialise()`, `pin()`, the `-P -B` re-exec, the runtime-root ladder, the
refusal taxonomy, the exit-code contract, the CLI surface and CP4B's
admissibility model, clause table and fixtures are unchanged in the text it
read, and that neither of its findings touches any of them. It answered the
two things revision 43 asked of it by building rather than reading. It
implemented the command-line half from that half's own row alone — the two
prefixes, the six command names, the bracket exclusion and the newly
declared text model — read no figure from the document, and reproduced the
published sequence site for site under every reading the row names, then
answered the second ask directly: **there is no fourth unstated convention
in that row**. The row is finished, and revision 44 does not edit it.

**Both findings are accepted in full; neither is rejected, deferred or
narrowed**, and every premise was reproduced against this repository before
its row was written. Both are the same defect one instrument over from where
round 42 found it, and both sit in the paragraphs revision 42 wrote to close
round 41's finding.

**The class is now stated as one generalisation rather than rediscovered per
instrument.** This document declares recognisers over its own text, and each
time a new clause *uses* one, the text model it needed turns out not to have
been declared. Round 42 found it for the command-line half's extraction,
under the component pin's clause (d). Round 43 found it for the partition
pin's clause (v) — whose prose-count authority was declared by description
plus one illustrative quotation — and, one notch weaker, for the component
pin's own region reader. The generalisation revision 44 adopts and applies
everywhere at once is the round's own: **every recogniser this document
declares must state the text model it runs over, and an illustrative
quotation is not a text model.** The round names the four recognisers left
under-declared — clause (v)'s section rule and its prose-count rule, and the
component pin's region-finding and delimiting rules — and this revision
declares all four.

**Neither finding is a figure being wrong.** The five prose counts are 3, 2,
2, 1 and 1 in the document as published and were before this revision; the
three regions carry the sequences they claim. What was wrong is that the
only build the declarations supported could not reach them — a required
suite red against a correct document, or a case that cannot fail. That is
this document's own recurring shape, and it is why a round that reads the
sentences certifies the sub-assertion green, as round 42 did, while a round
that runs the rule finds nothing to run.

| Finding | Disposition (each premise reproduced against this repository before the row was written) |
|---|---|
| **`OPUS-R43-B1`** (Blocking) — clause (v) declares its prose-count authority by description plus one illustrative quotation whose form occurs nowhere inside the window the clause reads, so a build reading the declaration finds no prose count in any of the five sections | **Accepted in full, and both halves of the finding were reproduced by extraction before this row was written.** The illustrated forms are `**3 Blocking**` and `**1 Blocking**`; inside rounds 34 through 38 they occur **zero** times, and `**2 Blocking**` occurs zero times anywhere in the document — the five sections use `**3 Blocking, 1 Important and 2 Optional**` and its siblings, and the illustrated form lives only at rounds 12, 15, 18 and 19, outside the window. The second half reproduces too: the declared section heading matched for equality is satisfied by none of rounds 34 through 38, every one of which appends a stage parenthetical, and by every round from 39 on, which append none. **Both authorities are restated as forms where the clause is declared**, beside the row recogniser that was already spelled out to the character, and the row recogniser gains its own text model in the same edit so the clause states one per step: the section is found by a heading **prefix** match with the parenthetical outside the match, over lines; the rows are found over lines, a Markdown table row being a single line by construction; and the prose count is *the first bold span, over whitespace-normalised text, whose text begins `<integer> Blocking` or `no Blocking`*, `no` read as zero. **Round 38's own rule is stated as part of it and needs no special case**: that section states two counts, local round 38's `APPROVE` with nothing Blocking is unbolded and therefore not a candidate, and the first *matching* span is the external reviewer's — the count the clause wants, since it is the external stage that puts round 38 in the window. **The coverage is declared rather than assumed**, which is what the finding asks for given that the window is read from the sentence and has moved once: run over every disposition section, the recogniser answers at rounds 12 and 15 onward and covers all three bolded notations, and rounds 1 through 11, 13 and 14 state their counts unbolded and are a **declared gap with declared behaviour** — a section with no match is a failure of clause (v) naming the round, never a skip, since a skip-on-no-match build is the cannot-fail shape the clause exists to stop. Re-run from the declaration as it now reads: five sections found by the prefix rule, prose counts extracting **by rule** to 3, 2, 2, 1 and 1, agreeing round for round with the nine `(Blocking)` rows, set equality unchanged. **The instantiation set gains the two cases the finding identifies**, since none of the five existing ones exercised the prose reader at all: a fourth failing case whose row set is correct but whose prose count for one round disagrees with it, which the third failing case cannot substitute for because that one is discriminated by the row recogniser and stays red with the prose reader deleted; and a third false-positive stating its counts in a second and third declared notation, which is red under a build that implements only the notation the live window uses |
| **`OPUS-R43-I1`** (Important) — the component pin declares a text model for its figures but not for finding or delimiting its regions, and R2's opening literal occurs on no line of this document | **Accepted in full, and the measurement reproduces exactly.** R2's declared opening literal wraps mid-sentence in the published text, so line-wise it occurs **zero** times while R1's and R3's occur twice each; under whitespace normalisation all three occur twice. A build that searches for the opening literals the way the delimiting rule was phrased — over lines, since the rule names blank lines and line beginnings — locates R1 and R3, never locates R2, and takes clause (a) red and clause (c) unrunnable against a correct document. **One text model is declared for all three steps** rather than for the figure extraction alone, in the form the finding asks for and stated as three definitions a build can implement: a blank line, a block as a maximal run of non-blank lines, and a block's normalised text with each line's own start offset known by construction — which is exactly what lets the delimiter's two boundaries survive normalisation instead of being destroyed by it. **The delimiter is restated rather than changed**: a region runs from its opening literal to the end of its block, stopping earlier at the first line-start after its own line whose line begins with a list-item marker, and a region opening on a table row runs to that row's line end. The blank-line half of the old phrasing is now the block boundary and the list-item half is the line-start test, and the rule answers the same three spans it did at revision 43. **Region discovery gains the positional requirement that was doing the work implicitly**: each opening literal must sit at the start of the object its region names — a table row's first cell, a block, a list item's content — which is what excludes the three quotations of those same literals in the declaration's own bullets, each inside a code span mid-item. Re-run over all three regions from the declaration as it now reads: R1 answers **7**, R2 and R3 both answer 8, 24, 2, 7, 7, 16, 7, and all four clauses are green. The grading is accepted as the finding states it — Important rather than Blocking, because the adjacent sentence's *"over whitespace-normalised text"* gives a careful implementer the reading that recovers R2, where `OPUS-R43-B1` has no such rescue |

## Plan review round 44 — disposition

Round 44 reviewed bundle `184d99e6…` at plan revision 44 and returned
`REVISE` with **1 Blocking, 1 Important and 1 Optional** finding — and it is
the **seventh consecutive round to find nothing in the design**: its
architecture section records that `materialise()`, `pin()`, the `-P -B`
re-exec, the runtime-root ladder, the refusal taxonomy, the exit-code
contract, the CLI surface and CP4B's admissibility model, clause table and
fixtures are unchanged in the text it read, that the diff touches seven paths
and none of them frozen, and that none of its three findings touches any of
it. It answered both of revision 44's asks by building rather than by
reading. It implemented clause (v) from its three new declarations alone —
the heading prefix over lines, the row recogniser over lines, the bold-span
prose recogniser over whitespace-normalised text — and the run answers five
sections, prose counts of three, two, two, one and one, and nine `(Blocking)`
ids set-equal to the sentence's own enumeration, with round 38's two counts
resolving to the external reviewer's under no special case. It built the
component pin's region reader from the declared block model and located R2 —
whose opening literal is on no line of this document — delimited all three
regions at the spans revision 44 records, and excluded the three code-span
quotations by the positional rule. **Both of round 43's repairs are
therefore verified by construction, and neither is edited again**: clause
(v), the component pin's region reader and the command-line half's row stand
as round 44 rebuilt them.

**All three findings are accepted in full; none is rejected, deferred or
narrowed**, and every premise was reproduced against this repository before
its row was written.

**What revision 44 got wrong was not a repair but a claim of closure, and
that is the finding this revision exists to apply.** Round 43's
generalisation — every recogniser this document declares must state the text
model it runs over, and an illustrative quotation is not a text model —
was correct and revision 44 applied it correctly and completely to the four
instruments round 43 named. But round 43 enumerated those four by looking at
the two pins, where its own findings were, and revision 44 adopted that list
as the whole family and said so. The family was never enumerated. **A
generalisation applied to a list is not applied to a class**, and the two
halves that still recognise this document's own prose were never counted —
one of them carrying the identical defect in its identical shape.

**The enumeration is therefore closed by construction in this revision
rather than inherited from a finding's list**, which is round 44's own
acceptance criterion 9 and the correction of the error it found. Every
recogniser this document declares, with the text model each now states:

| Recogniser | Declared text model | Declared in |
|---|---|---|
| the **complexity** half's occurrence extraction and its superseded-figure exclusion | blocks, a table row a block of its own, a sentence cut at a full stop and a space; figures include bare bold decimals and polarity is read from the word `today` | revision 45 |
| the **exit-code** half's two-sided table extraction | lines: the table located by its own heading, a row split into cells, meanings compared after formatting is reduced to text | revision 45 |
| the **round-count** half | the document's text with whitespace normalised to single spaces, because an occurrence that wraps is one occurrence | revision 37 |
| the **command-line** half | code spans and fenced lines, backtick pairing scoped to the paragraph, whitespace normalised, a span's text stripped | revision 43 |
| the **partition pin**'s occurrence recogniser | sentences over whitespace-normalised text, an occurrence being sentence-initial and running to the first full stop after its literal | revision 41 |
| clause (v)'s **section** step | lines, the heading matched by prefix with the stage parenthetical outside the match | revision 44 |
| clause (v)'s **row** step | lines, a Markdown table row being a single line by construction | revision 44 |
| clause (v)'s **prose-count** step | the section's text with whitespace normalised, the first bold span whose text opens with an integer or `no` before `Blocking` | revision 44 |
| the **component pin**'s region discovery | the block model, with each opening literal required to sit at the start of the object its region names | revision 44 |
| the same pin's region **delimiter** | the block model: to the block's end, stopping at the first line-start list-item marker, a table-row region ending at its own line's end | revision 44 |

Two properties this document also carries are deliberately **not** in this
family, and saying so is what makes the enumeration closed rather than
merely long: the `KNOWN_PHASES` equality and the command-file partition each
enumerate a **closed external artifact** with a literal membership test and
neither recognises anything in prose — which is the same criterion the
out-of-scope row states, and the reason revision 38 moved the exit-code
half's *subject* onto one. After this revision's two declarations there is no
recogniser left whose text model is unstated, so there is no eighth
instrument of this kind for a round 45 to find one in — and, unlike revision
44's claim, that is a statement about an enumerated family rather than about
a list inherited from a round.

| Finding | Disposition (each premise reproduced against this repository before the row was written) |
|---|---|
| **`OPUS-R44-B1`** (Blocking) — the complexity half's superseded-figure exclusion is declared by description plus one illustrative quotation whose polarity is the opposite of all three sites the exclusion acts on, so built from the declaration the half is red at two of them against a correct document | **Accepted in full, and every figure in the finding was reproduced by extraction before this row was written.** The polarity claim reproduces exactly: the convention's worked example writes the current figure in this half's own occurrence form and the superseded one bare, while at all three live marked pairs — revision 3's challenge question about CP4, CP6's *"revision 1 made this one checkpoint"* sentence, and round 3's CP4B disposition row — the only figure in the occurrence form is the **superseded** one and the current half is a bare bold decimal that no declared recogniser read. The quoted form occurs twice in the document and at none of those three sites. **Both readings the declaration supports were built and run.** Under the strict one — figures only in this half's own occurrence form, the pair required to be for the same checkpoint — no marked pair is found at any of the three sites, all three superseded figures stay in scope, and the half is red at **three** of them. Under the co-occurrence reading the remaining wording licenses, which is the build the finding reports, six occurrences leave scope, the half is red at the **two** the finding names, and **five** live figures go unchecked — CP6's and CP6B's at both sites that state them, and CP4's in round 3's disposition row. The finding writes four there; the extraction answers five, and the difference does not touch its conclusion, since the reading is the one round 19's I3 rejected under either count. Both of this document's named failure shapes are therefore present at once, in the same half. **The repair is the one the finding asks for, and it is three declarations rather than a tuned match set**: a text model over blocks with a table row a block of its own and a sentence cut at a full stop and a space; a figure and polarity rule in which bare bold decimals **are** figures, a figure is attributed to the nearest `CP` token in its sentence (preceding, else following, matched maximally so `CP4B` is never read as `CP4`), and a figure is presented as current when the word `today` follows it; and a declared coverage in which every occurrence resolves to exactly one of excluded, out of scope or in scope, with an unknown checkpoint a **failure naming the site** rather than a skip. The block model is not decoration: at one of the three pairs the current half sits on the line after the superseded one, so a line-oriented build cannot see that pair at all. **Re-run from those declarations over this revision's published text**: thirteen occurrences, three excluded, one out of scope for naming no checkpoint, nine in scope, all nine agreeing with the registry — the classification the row has claimed since revision 19, now reached by rule instead of by reading. **The instantiation set gains the one case none of the three existing ones can reach**, for the reason the finding gives: none of them fixes a polarity, so a current-first build satisfies all three. The new fixture writes its marked pair superseded-first with an off-registry occurrence and a bare bold decimal current half, and must **not** fail. The grade is accepted as stated — this is `OPUS-R43-B1`'s shape one instrument over, and the precedent for grading it is `OPUS-R43-B1` itself |
| **`OPUS-R44-I1`** (Important) — the exit-code half declares neither how a build locates the Exit codes table in either document nor how a row becomes a `(code, meaning)` pair, and the meanings carry formatting a set comparison is sensitive to | **Accepted in full.** Confirmed against the live table by extraction: **four** of its ten meanings carry inline formatting — one bold and three carrying code spans — so an ADR stating the same meanings with the emphasis rendered differently takes a required suite red against a correct ADR, which is this document's own first named failure shape. The three steps are declared in the row: the table is located in **each** document by the first heading whose text is exactly `Exit codes`, the table being the run of table lines after it with its header and delimiter excluded; a row is a pair when it splits into exactly two cells and the first parses as a decimal integer, and a row that does not is a failure naming the line; codes are compared as integers and meanings after `**`, `*` and backtick runs are removed and whitespace is collapsed. A document in which the locating rule finds nothing fails the half **naming the document**, never contributing an empty set — the cannot-fail shape this half was rescoped in revision 38 to escape, which is exactly where an unstated locating rule would have reintroduced it. The grading is accepted for the finding's own reason: CP9 writes the ADR and this test in one checkpoint, so an implementer controls both sides and can make them agree by construction, where `OPUS-R44-B1`'s authority is this document's own already-written prose |
| **`OPUS-R44-O1`** (Optional) — the `withdraw_bundle` line citation is the only imprecise one of the twenty-one into frozen tooling, and its range stops before the rename it is cited for | **Accepted and applied at both sites.** Verified in the frozen file: `withdraw_bundle`'s `def` is at `workflow_fingerprint.py:2388` and its `return` at `:2449`, while the cited range began on the third line of its docstring and ended three lines before the `os.rename` the citation is offered for, at `:2444`. Both statements — the CP4B evidence paragraph and round 5's I2 disposition row — now cite `:2388-2449`. The finding's own reason for raising it is the reason it is applied rather than deferred: the other twenty citations land on exact boundaries, so the convention is precise and this one citation was the exception |

denylist paragraph above: a file carries the guard when its text contains

(revision 50, local round 49's `OPUS-R49-B1`, required acceptance criterion
1, superseding revision 49's wording; revision 51, local round 50's
`OPUS-R50-B1`, required acceptance criteria 1 and 2, adding the sixth
source below and making this the sole statement of the enumeration): a
predicate is category-(B) — belongs in this table, closed or open —
exactly when it must **locate, delimit, or extract** from prose (this
document's own text or a frozen `.claude/commands/*.md`/
`docs/ACTIVE_MILESTONE.md` file), an external process's byte stream, a
Markdown document, source code, **or the Controller's own observable
output** — a raised `ControllerError`'s human sentence, the rendered
values carried in its `evidence` mapping, or the CLI's stdout/stderr —
**or text the Controller itself composes or is handed as a runtime
argument**, of which the worker `task` string passed to `claude -p` is the
only current instance. This fifth source is what revision 49's wording
omitted: `evidence` is a typed attribute, and revision 49's exclusion
clause read "a typed attribute is excluded" as reaching the values that
attribute carries, when it only ever meant to exclude the attribute's own
declared shape. This sixth source is what revision 50's five-source
wording omitted: a `task` string is input the Controller sends to a
worker process, the opposite direction from "an external process's byte
stream", and is neither prose, a Markdown document, source code, nor the
Controller's own output — so CP5's task-token scan was excluded by a
criterion the amended CP5 row itself contradicted (`OPUS-R50-B1`). A
predicate that only checks an exit code, tuple/set membership, or file
existence is excluded, never category-(B), regardless of how many such
checks a checkpoint declares.

enumeration above** (revision 52, required acceptance criterion 1,
`OPUS-R51-B1`): a predicate that *was* category-(B) under this criterion,
and that a later revision resolved by replacing its text read with a
declared structured channel — a fixed literal held in a typed attribute or
an `evidence` key, an enum — **leaves the family**. It is not thereby
closed within it: the verb-gate above excludes an equality against a
declared field's value exactly as it excludes the field's own container,
so a predicate resolved this way now reads a value rather than locating,
delimiting or extracting anything from text. Record such a predicate, with
the revision that moved it, in neither the closed nor the open column —
one instance of this general rule each time it applies, not a growing
enumeration of named exceptions. This is different from a predicate that
was never category-(B) to begin with — CP3's `KNOWN_PHASES` set equality
and CP4's command-file partition property are that shape from the outset
and are excluded, not relisted, for exactly the reason the header
paragraph above already states — the rule here is for an item that *was*
carried in this table's closed column and is repaired out of it.

**This walk closes every predicate `OPUS-R46-B1` and `OPUS-R49-B2` named,
completes coverage to all eleven rows (`OPUS-R49-I2`), and says so rather
than rounding up to closure.** The open column is longer than the finding
sets that produced it, because the walk is performed independently against
the actual checkpoint text rather than bounded to any one round's own
citations — the discipline `/apply-plan-review`'s own validation step and
this document's repeated acceptance criteria on this walk ask for. None of
the open items is a new checkpoint, a new requirement, a new complexity, or
a new test file: every one is a text model missing from a predicate this
document already declares. Challenge question 9, below, states this
plainly rather than claiming a clean design round also means a closed
apparatus.

narrowed**, except that `OPUS-R47-B2`'s own row-5 walk surfaces a case this

| Finding | Disposition (each premise reproduced against this repository before the row was written) |
|---|---|
| **`OPUS-R47-B1`** (Blocking) — the component pin's clause (a) is red against revision 47's own published text: a figure edit's own line wrap put a bare `46. ` at a line start inside R2's block, which the delimiter's unqualified list-item-marker test reads as an ordered-list item, truncating R2 to six figures | **Accepted in full, and reproduced before being applied.** Confirmed: R2's block, read to the first line beginning with a decimal and `. `, stops at line 4723 (`"…unmoved through revision"`), one line before its own survivor count — six figures, not seven, exactly as the finding measures. The delimiter's list-item marker gains the qualification CommonMark itself already states for an ordered list that interrupts a paragraph — the decimal must read `1` — rather than admitting any decimal, which closes the recurrence class rather than only this occurrence: a rewrap alone would have left `48`, `49` and every later revision counter free to reproduce the identical defect at whichever line a future figure edit happens to wrap it to. R2's wrapped sentence is also rewritten, in the same edit, so no line in any of the three regions begins with a decimal and `. ` today; re-run after both edits, R1 is immune by construction, R3 carries no such line and is unchanged, and R2 runs uninterrupted to its true end. All four clauses are green against the published text: (a) R2 and R3 both seven long and identical; (b) R1's `7` equals their seventh element; (c) 2+8+7=17 and 8+17=25; (d) the sequence equals the command-line half's own extraction |

CP4's own denylist derivation is untouched and re-verified at three matching files with `recover-implementation-provenance.md:79` still excluded, since form (iii) is scoped to property 5 alone. Row 5, walked per the finding's own acceptance criterion 4, does **not** resolve under the corrected model either, for a different reason than row 3's — its declared branch is a two-line span that only references step 5 by number rather than containing step 5's own text — and is recorded as an open item in the walk table above rather than patched, since neither offered repair (teaching the branch model to follow a cross-reference, or restating row 5's branch to point at step 5 directly) is decidable without touching every other `governing_version=` row this schema might add |

second time in two rounds this document's verification apparatus has found
the same shape one level apart.** `OPUS-R46-B2` was a figure gone stale

**What this round changes about the shape of the loop, addressed directly
in the "Architecture and maintainability concerns" section of round 51's
own feedback.** `OPUS-R51-B1` is not a new class of defect; it is
`OPUS-R49-B1`'s and `OPUS-R50-B1`'s class — a repair that is itself
inconsistent with the rule it repairs — arriving through a third door in as
many rounds, each time inside the repair for the round before. Round 51's
own reviewer named the cause: the walk is a plan-stage artifact auditing
implementation-stage obligations, and every one of its open items is a
detail an implementer needs when writing a test, not a decision that must
be settled before implementation may begin. Required acceptance criterion
4, applied above ("Open items moved to implementation obligations"), acts
on that diagnosis: the roughly twenty open items become 24 numbered
requirements in the mapping, attached to the checkpoints that own them,
verified by count (24 before, 24 after); the plan-stage walk keeps the
criterion, the closed column, and the excluded-family rule, and points at
the mapping for what remains open rather than re-stating it. This does not
by itself guarantee the next round finds nothing — the closed column,
where `OPUS-R49-B1`, `OPUS-R50-B1` and `OPUS-R51-B1` all in fact lived, is
unchanged in shape — but it removes the roughly-twenty-item open column as
a second, larger surface for the same defect shape to keep recurring on.

named rather than left inferable** (round 64's `O1`): since
`.ai-review/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md` is overwritten by every round
that follows it, `EXT-PLAN-R62-O1`'s own text survives nowhere on disk
today except inside this section, which is itself built from round 63's
quotation of round 62's finding — a chain of two quotations, this one and
round 63's, and this document is the only place either link is still
readable.

Round 62 was the **only** round in this item's history to close both
stages. `LOCAL_MODEL_PLAN_REVIEW` returned `APPROVE` at round 62 against
bundle `c09c2c51…` / content id `fc3cadb4…`; `MANUAL_EXTERNAL_PLAN_REVIEW`
returned `APPROVE` at its round 1 against the same bundle; and
`/approve-review plan` recorded `plan_approval.status: CURRENT` on the
strength of both. That approval is now `SUPERSEDED` by the
`/request-plan-amendment` this amendment runs under, and the ledger keeps
it in `amendment_history[0].superseded_plan_approval`.

| Finding | Disposition | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **`EXT-PLAN-R62-O1`** (Optional, manual external stage) — resolve CP6B's `REQ-31` early, and keep the chosen verifier rule single-source | **Accepted as advice, and deliberately not acted on in this amendment.** Re-verified at revision 64: `REQ-31` is still open in the mapping, assigned to `CP6B` alone, and names the two remedies property 5's own row-5 walk already states — teach the branch-span model to follow a *"steps N-M execute"* cross-reference, or restate row 5's branch to point at step 5's text directly. **The one finding is accepted; none is rejected.** This is this work item's
first `MANUAL_EXTERNAL_PLAN_REVIEW` round since round 38, and the first of
either stage to find something in the amendment's own supported-baseline
design rather than in this document's account of itself: every finding
from round 63 through round 66 was a citation, a count, a stale claim about
a past round, or a rule this document had already stated but not yet
enforced consistently. This one is different in kind — it agrees the B2
bootstrap architecture is sound and asks nothing about it; it finds a gap
in the *admission rule* revision 64 wrote to resolve `B6`, one that
survived four further local rounds because none of those rounds' own
properties were built to see it.

| Finding | Disposition | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **`I1`** (Important) — admitting the whole `2.5.x` line is not fail-closed against a future patch that changes an already-known command's or phase's semantics while leaving `KNOWN_PHASES`, the command-file inventory and the two-directional properties over them unchanged; `2.5.x` admission must not mean "trust every future patch solely because its major/minor version matches" | **Accepted in full, and reproduced against the design before it was changed**: `SUPPORTED_WORKFLOW_LINE`'s bullet and the "why admitting a line is fail-closed" paragraph (revision 64) argue only that an unmodelled phase or command is refused or unselectable — true, and unaffected — and say nothing about a modelled one whose behaviour moves under its own name, which neither two-directional property (each a check over *names*) can see. **The repair is the design the finding's own first acceptable option names, per required acceptance criteria 1 and 2**: `VALIDATED_WORKFLOW_RELEASES = {"2.5.1"}` becomes the actual admission gate — an exact-membership check, not a line match — with `SUPPORTED_WORKFLOW_LINE` kept as a necessary pre-filter and diagnostic classifier only. `2.5.0`, a real, currently-distributed release this document never measured, is now refused on the same footing as an unreleased future `2.5.2` — both are "known line, unvalidated release", evidence that is asserted to read differently from a wrong-line refusal. Growing the set is stated as a deliberate, named act — re-derive the three inventories and the seven baseline-verification suites, then add the release by name in a plan revision — never automatic from a parsed major/minor match, which is the finding's own required boundary. **Required acceptance criterion 3** (re-derive every affected statement rather than patch isolated prose) is carried out at every site the old rule's fail-closed argument or its test enumeration touched: the "Supported Workflow baseline" policy section, CP2 step 5's admission rule, the baseline-predicate test enumeration, and CP2's registry/mapping complexity. **Required acceptance criterion 5** (bounded scope) is honoured by construction: no Controller behaviour outside Workflow-version admission is touched, and the B2 bootstrap architecture this round separately found coherent is not reopened or implemented here | the "Supported Workflow baseline" policy section's `VALIDATED_WORKFLOW_RELEASES` bullet and its rewritten fail-closed argument; CP2 step 5's admission rule; the baseline-predicate test enumeration (four cases → seven); the `## Checkpoints` complexity narrative's new revision-68 paragraph; `REQ-43` and `REQ-T18B` in the mapping; CP2's registry complexity (4 → 5) and its regenerated `## Checkpoints` table row |

**The one missing test is added, and it is the case the six pre-existing
baseline-predicate cases cannot exercise between them** (required
acceptance criterion 4): a fixture repository whose `.claude/commands/`
tree and `KNOWN_PHASES` block are byte-identical copies of the validated
`2.5.1` reference tree — so every inventory CP2, CP3 and CP4 read is,

CP9's unaffected live-Manager integration test.

**Required acceptance criterion 6** (regenerate the bundle and return to

the time.

1. **Is the immutable-execution root the right shape, or is it too much
   machinery for Generation 1?** It adds snapshot materialisation, a
   content digest, a re-exec and a new refusal class to the checkpoint
   that was meant to be the small one. The honest alternative is the
   eager-load-only model, which is cheaper and which this plan keeps as
   its *second* argument — but which rests on proving a negative about
   every future import and resource read. A reviewer who thinks the
   negative is provable enough should say so, because that would let CP1
   drop back to 3.
2. **Does the re-exec actually terminate, now that the argument has been
   rebuilt?** Round 32 answered the previous version of this question *no*,
   and it was the right question to have asked: revision 32 bounded the exec
   from the branch structure alone while leaving the child's import root to
   the invoking working directory, and the failure was an unbounded exec
   loop rather than any of the three outcomes the design named. Revision 33
   rests the bound on two facts — the import root `-P` constructs, and the
   branch `SOURCE_PIN.json` selects — and adds a refusal-only exec-depth
   fail-safe behind them. Round 33 ran that mechanism rather than reading
   it and answered **yes** — exec count exactly 1, `safe_path` true in the
   child, `sys.path[0]` the snapshot, an inherited hostile `PYTHONPATH`
   neutralised by assignment — and separately confirmed that the fail-safe
   can only refuse and never admit. So the open questions are the ones
   revision 34 created around it. Round 34 answered one of them and it was
   the one nobody had asked: the bound holds, but the **snapshot** did not,
   because importing it modified it, so a correct build refused on run 1 and
   refused permanently from run 2. Revision 35 answers that with `-B` and a
   digest declared total, and round 35 ran it twice from a clean checkout
   and confirmed both — the snapshot survives execution and is reused. But
   round 35 also found the answer incomplete in the way this question asked:
   there **was** a second thing a pinned run writes into its own snapshot,
   and it was the temporary created by the very rewrite the question named as
   excluded. Revision 36 moves that temporary out of the directory entirely,
   so the file set is now literally constant under reuse and the exclusion
   set is a closed set of one. **Round 36 was asked whether "constant" was
   true rather than merely declared, went looking for a third write site,
   and could not name one** — the pinned child's own import is closed by
   `-B` in the argv, anything the child launches is closed by CP5's explicit
   `env=` with `PYTHONPATH` removed, and a human's direct diagnostic run is
   closed by the stated `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, with the consequence of
   omitting it written down rather than left to be discovered. Two rounds
   each found exactly one write site and the third found none, which is the
   strongest evidence this property has. **What revision 37 owes instead is
   the instrument**, because round 36's answer was that the file set is
   constant in fact and that nothing *tested* it: test 4's third run is now
   an interrupted rewrite asserting the snapshot gains no file. A reviewer
   should check that this fixture really is red against the same-directory
   rule where revision 36's planted-file fixture was not — that failure is
   the defect this revision exists to correct, and a repair for a
   discrimination failure that does not itself discriminate would be the
   worst possible outcome of this round. A reviewer who can still name a
   fourth write site should. The
   residual
   questions from revision 34 stand alongside it: is `exec_depth` read early
   enough, and is the record's newly-stated write point right on the paths
   that refuse as well as the paths that succeed; and is test 2's instrument
   — *a call to `cli.main` that returns is proof no `execv` happened* —
   airtight, or does it merely hold for the in-process invocation it is
   written for?
3. **Is `--allow-dirty-source` still a hole?** Its meaning changed rather
   than being removed: the run still executes from an immutable snapshot,
   but one made from uncommitted bytes, identified by digest with a `null`
   commit. That is the external finding's own second remedy, and it is
   what keeps CP9's own integration test runnable in the checkpoint that
   writes it. A reviewer may hold that any dirty-source execution is
   unacceptable and that CP9 should clone-and-commit instead.
4. **Does the generation rule still hold for a worktree-sourced
   snapshot?** The plan says yes: a `"worktree"` snapshot still resolves
   its generation from the origin's committed `HEAD`, so pinned and
   approved read the same bytes and round 1's composition defect stays
   unreachable. This is the composition most likely to be wrong, because
   it is the one place the new model and the oldest fix meet.
5. **Is CP8's step 7 a real proof now?** Round 32 measured it and said no:
   it reconstructed the child's import root as `[source_root]`, which is the
   assumption `OPUS-R32-B1` falsified, so it would have reported the
   snapshot whatever the child did. Revision 33 has the child record its own
   `sys.path` and runs the probe under exactly that. Challenge whether
   recording at `cli.main` entry is early enough, and whether a recorded
   path is still a measurement of the process that later imports — the
   honest residual weakness is that it captures `sys.path` at one instant,
   so a module that mutated `sys.path` afterwards would not appear in it.
   CP1's no-late-read scan is the independent argument against that, and a
   reviewer who holds it insufficient should say so and name what would
   suffice. Revision 34 changes one clause of it: the *"no entry inside the
   clone"* assertion now states why it is satisfiable here — step 2's
   `--runtime-dir <tmp>` puts the snapshot outside the clone — where CP1
   test 1, at the default runtime root, must use the narrower form. A
   reviewer should check that the two forms are consistent rather than
   merely different, since one document now states the containment property
   two ways on purpose. Revision 35 changes step 2's command line — the
   global `--runtime-dir` now precedes `run` — so the probe's premise is
   unchanged but the invocation that establishes it is not; a reviewer should
   check that the corrected line still selects the clone as the origin and
   still puts the snapshot outside it. Revision 36 makes the same premise
   explicit at steps 3 and 6, whose record paths were `.controller/<name>`
   while step 2 passes `--runtime-dir <tmp>` — they now read `<tmp>/`, and
   step 3 states once that `--runtime-dir` is ladder row 1 so no
   `.controller/` exists in the clone at all. A reviewer should check that
   this is the same fact step 7 rests on rather than a second, similar one,
   and that no other step in CP8 or CP9 still names a record path the
   fixture it runs under does not create. Revision 37 answers the last of
   those: round 36 found step **7** still reading `.controller/identity.json`
   under the same `--runtime-dir <tmp>` fixture, so it now reads `<tmp>/`
   too, and the convention that makes the generic spelling legible elsewhere
   moves out of step 3 to the runtime-root ladder, where a reader meets the
   tree. Step 3's wait condition, which revision 36's own insertion split in
   two, is made whole again. **Round 37 answered the last open clause and
   it is closed**: it resolved every `.controller/` occurrence in this
   document against that convention and found none of them a fixture path —
   the Controller's own `.gitignore` entry, CP1 test 1's named
   default-editable mode, the explicit `<origin>/` write and test 6(a)'s
   named row-3 failure mode are all genuinely row 3. Revision 38 changes
   nothing in CP8. What it changes nearby is `status`'s **empty-root
   report**, which now states what it measures, because the reporting
   process writes `identity.json` into that root before its own body runs; a
   reviewer should check that this answer is consistent with CP9's surface
   row for `status` and with CP1 test 6(a)'s two new assertions, rather than
   a third statement of the same rule. Revision 39 changes nothing in CP8
   or anywhere near it: its single mechanism change is in CP4B's evidence
   layer, which CP8 does not read.
6. **Re-derive the automatic-action/user-gate partition from the frozen
   sources now in the bundle**, which is the whole point of including
   them: **seventeen** command files, the two denylist recognisers (3 and
   3 members, **union 4**), the **twenty** phases, the six automatic
   triples, the seven `ExpectedOutcome` rows, and the exact agreement
   between CP4's automatic rows and CP6B's table. This plan asserts all of
   it; nothing but the frozen files can confirm it. **Revision 64 is the
   first round where these figures are re-derived against a release the
   plan did not ship with**, so a reviewer should re-read them against the
   *installed* tree rather than against the bundle's own narrative — which
   is exactly the check that was not performed between the Manager update
   and round 63.
7. **Is `VALIDATED_WORKFLOW_RELEASES` the right admission rule, and is the
   line predicate still earning its place beside it?** **Re-derived at
   revision 69** (round 68's `I1`): through revision 67 this item asked the
   opposite question, describing revision 64's `2.5`-line predicate as the
   choice in force and "a closed set that each release joins once measured"
   as the narrower alternative *not* taken. Revision 68 took that
   alternative. `SUPPORTED_INSTALLATIONS`, the identifier this item used to
   name the superseded pair-set, no longer names anything in the current
   design; its only remaining occurrences are in frozen disposition rows,
   where they are provenance.

   **The choice now in force** is two-tier, and the "Supported Workflow
   baseline" section derives it: `VALIDATED_WORKFLOW_RELEASES = {"2.5.1"}`
   is the admission gate, an exact-membership check; `SUPPORTED_WORKFLOW_LINE
   = "2.5"` is retained as a necessary pre-filter and diagnostic classifier
   that lets a refusal say *wrong line* rather than *not yet validated*, and
   is never a second gate a validated release must independently clear.
   Round 67's `I1` is what forced it: the two two-directional properties
   compare **names**, so a future `2.5.x` that renamed nothing and added
   nothing but changed an already-known command's persisted-state contract
   would have been admitted silently under the bare line predicate.

   **What is still open to challenge, stated as a choice rather than a
   derivation.** Three things:

   - **The accepted cost.** Exact membership converts every Manager update
     inside the line from a no-op into a plan revision — re-derive the three
     inventories, re-run the seven baseline-verification suites, add the
     release by name. The plan accepts that cost deliberately. A reviewer
     may hold it too high for a Generation 1 whose own repository the
     Manager has already updated mid-flight once, and should say so.
   - **Whether the pre-filter earns its keep.** It admits nothing the
     admission gate does not, so it is pure diagnosis: two distinguishable
     refusal-evidence shapes instead of one. A reviewer may hold that a
     single refusal shape is simpler and that carrying a second constant to
     improve a message is machinery this checkpoint does not need.
   - **Where the cost actually lands, which is not in CP2.** Round 68's
     `B1` found it in CP9: `REQ-T18` installs a real Workflow release, and
     under exact membership it can no longer mean "whatever the Manager
     holds as newest". Revision 69 pins that fixture to a validated release
     and adds `REQ-T18C` to make an unvalidated one fail by name (`REQ-T18`
     step 2 and step 3b). The consequence is that this repository's
     integration evidence and this repository's *installed* release can
     diverge the next time the Manager updates. That divergence is stated
     and made audible rather than removed, and a reviewer may hold that the
     wrong trade — that live evidence should always track the installation
     even at the price of a refusal — and should say so here rather than
     at CP9, since it is this policy that decides it.

   **And is supporting both profiles right, against refusing all but
   `full`?** Unchanged by revision 68 and re-checked at revision 69: the
   plan measured that `runtime` installs the identical
   command and tooling surface and admits it on that basis, re-measured at
   revision 64. Refusing it would be safer and less useful; the plan chose
   useful-and-measured, and pins the measurement with a fixture rather
   than a sentence. Note that `SUPPORTED_PROFILES` is genuinely a set of
   values rather than a line, so the round-67 objection does not reach it.
8. **Artifacts declaration** — unchanged in classification since revision
   1; revision 35 adds no path. Adding files to `CONTEXT_FILES.txt` copies
   frozen bytes into the bundle for reading and changes no classification,
   since classification ranges over the diff, not over the bundle's
   context copies.
9. **Is the plan converging on its own commentary rather than its
   design?** Rounds 31 through 36 have now answered this from seven sides,
   and the answer keeps changing: twelve consecutive local rounds found
   nothing Blocking; then an external round found an evidence gap and a live
   invariant weakness; then the local stage, reviewing the mechanism those
   produced, found its central argument false; then the next local round,
   reviewing the repair, found the repair sound and the **evidence written to
   demonstrate it** defective in four of nine tests; and then round 34,
   building the mechanism from this document's own text and *running it
   twice*, found that it does not survive its own first execution; and then
   round 35, running that same mechanism twice again, found it **works** —
   and found instead that the two pieces of new material revision 35 wrote
   to close round 34 had themselves never been run. Revisions 32 through 36
   are all mechanism rather than marking.

   **Round 36 is the first of the five that changes the answer's direction
   rather than its depth, and revision 37 is written on that reading.** It
   re-derived every rule revision 36 wrote and ran each of them: the
   three-clause recogniser (seven recognised, seven parse, and stable under
   its own one ambiguity), the runtime-root ladder (exhaustive, and it
   survives the shared-user-state-root collision question this document put
   to it), and the closed-set-of-one claim (no third writer into a published
   snapshot exists, by three independently closed routes). All of it held.
   What it found instead was **bookkeeping**: one round count bumped in two
   of its three places, and one test fixture specified at a path that
   discriminates nothing. Neither touches `materialise()`, `pin()`, the
   re-exec, the ladder, the taxonomy, the CLI surface, any requirement, any
   checkpoint or any complexity — and revision 37 changes none of them. That
   is a different kind of finding from rounds 32–34, each of which went one
   layer deeper into the same mechanism, and from round 35, which found new
   material never run at all.

   **So the honest answer has changed to: the design has now been measured
   intact twice, and what keeps failing is this document's account of
   itself.** That is worth stating precisely rather than as a count, because
   the two readings recommend opposite things. Under the count — five
   consecutive rounds with a Blocking finding in the newest material — the
   pattern argument wins: this loop cannot add a repair without adding a
   defect, and the right move is to implement what is settled. Under the
   kind, rounds 35 and 36 both ran the mechanism and both found it working,
   and the remaining defects are single-clause corrections in prose about
   prose, which is exactly the surface the Generation 2 document-structure
   commitment exists to remove and which has no effect on what gets built.
   **Round 36's own recommendation was to treat revision 37 as the last plan
   revision**, and this document adopts that as the question it puts back
   rather than as a decision it makes for the reviewer.

   **What a reviewer should therefore do with this revision is specific.**
   Do not re-audit the mechanism a third time unless something in revision
   37 touched it — nothing did, and the diff is the evidence. Test the two
   claims this revision makes about its own repairs: that CP1 test 4's
   interrupted-rewrite fixture is genuinely **red** against the
   same-directory rule, where revision 36's planted-file fixture was green
   against both (a repair for a discrimination failure that does not itself
   discriminate is the one outcome that would make this round worse than
   useless); and that the round-count half, stated now over
   whitespace-normalised text, actually sees the wrapped occurrence that
   drifted. Then answer the standing question directly: **if this round
   finds only bookkeeping again, is any further plan revision buying
   anything?** A reviewer who re-runs this document's own rules and finds
   them green should say so plainly and say whether the item should go to
   the manual external stage on the strength of a design measured intact
   twice — because that, and not another repair, is what this loop is now
   waiting on.

   **Round 37 answered `no` to the first half and `not yet` to the second,
   and the reason cuts against the convergence argument rather than for
   it.** It found the design intact for a third consecutive round: nothing
   in that round asks for a change to `materialise()`, `pin()`, the
   re-exec, the ladder, the refusal taxonomy, the CLI surface, any
   requirement, any checkpoint, any complexity or any test count, and it
   verified all three of revision 37's substantive repairs by running them.
   But it also found the premise the whole argument rests on — *"the rules
   are now run rather than read"* — false of one of the four halves: the
   exit-code half had been red since revision 34 and was certified green
   three times by describing its occurrence set instead of extracting it. A
   recommendation to stop revising on the strength of a design measured
   intact twice would have rested partly on a measurement nobody took.

   **Revision 38 adopted round 37's recommendation as a decision rather than
   as a question — *the loop should end at revision 38 whatever round 38
   finds* — and round 38 falsified the premise that decision rested on.** The
   premise was a count: that the recent Blocking findings lived in the
   document-consistency apparatus or in claims about it, and none in the
   Controller. Two things are now true of it. It was **numerically wrong when
   written** (round 38's `EXT-PLAN-R38-O1`, applied above at the site that
   states it). Of the nine Blocking findings of rounds 34-38, **three** are
   in the document-consistency apparatus (`OPUS-R35-B1`, `OPUS-R36-B1`,
   `OPUS-R37-B1`), **one** is a required Controller test satisfied by the
   wrong fixture (`OPUS-R36-B2`), and **five** are in the Controller itself
   (`OPUS-R34-B1`, `OPUS-R34-B2`, `OPUS-R34-B3`, `OPUS-R35-B2`,
   `EXT-PLAN-R38-B1`). **This site carried
   revision 39's six-for-seven partition too, and revision 40 corrected it in
   the same revision as the disposition row so the bundle carries one
   partition rather than two** (local round 39's `OPUS-R39-I2`). **Revision 41
   states it in the one notation the partition pin extracts and names the
   window by its endpoints rather than as *the last seven*** (local round 40's
   `OPUS-R40-B1`): a window that moves with every round is a figure no reader
   can reproduce from the document in front of them, and the rounds after 38
   are read below rather than folded into it.

   **Revision 42 corrects the population those endpoints actually select, and
   the correction strengthens this reading rather than weakening it** (local
   round 41's `OPUS-R41-B1`). The seven ids revisions 38 through 41
   enumerated were the last seven *as of revision 38*; rounds 34-38 contain
   **nine**, so the two the rename silently dropped — `OPUS-R34-B1`, the
   immutable-execution mechanism refusing on its own first pinned run, and
   `OPUS-R34-B2`, the two required evidence runs exiting 2 against the
   Controller's own CLI contract — are restored, both to the **Controller**
   column. **The criterion this question turns on is re-stated on that count,
   and it reads the same way, more strongly.** The criterion is *stop when a
   round's findings are in this document's account of itself, and do not stop
   while a round's findings are in the Controller*, and its stated evidence
   is where recent Blocking findings land. The stale figure put three of
   seven in the Controller; the corrected one puts **five of nine**. The
   undercount therefore biased the criterion toward **stopping** — the
   direction `OPUS-R39-I2` already named as the costly one for an error in
   this figure to run — and correcting it moves the historical record
   *further* from the stopping clause rather than nearer to it. What actually
   decides the question is unchanged, and it is deliberately not this ratio:
   the criterion is evaluated against **the round in front of it**, not
   against the window's history, and rounds 39, 40 and 41 each found nothing
   in the design. The window's figure is history — it is what made *"stop
   after revision 38"* wrong on the day it was written — and revision 42
   states it correctly so that the record the criterion was derived from is
   not itself a miscount. And the premise was **falsified
   by the round it was written to pre-empt**: round 38 is the manual external
   stage, and its Blocking finding is in the Controller's evidence layer, not
   in this document's commentary about itself.

   **What that round found is the specific thing thirty-eight local rounds
   could not, and it is worth naming as a property of the two-stage
   protocol rather than as a defect.** `EXT-PLAN-R38-B1` is a *composition*
   defect: CP4B's arrival predicate, `/record-manual-plan-review`'s
   validation and `/apply-plan-review`'s validation are each individually
   consistent with the plan, and the defect exists only in the seam between
   the second and the third — a file the Controller admits, the ingesting
   command accepts, and the applying command the Controller then selects
   refuses. Every local round read this document against itself and the
   frozen files it cites; finding this one required reading two frozen
   commands **against each other** and noticing that their feedback
   contracts differ. That is the argument for the manual external stage
   existing, and it is the strongest evidence in this record that the local
   loop's convergence and the plan's correctness are different questions.

   **So revision 39 withdraws the "last revision whatever happens"
   commitment and replaces it with a criterion.** The apparatus argument is
   unchanged and still right — iterating a plan document to make its
   self-audit correct returns less than shipping the design, and revision
   38's reduction of the apparatus stands — but *"stop after revision N"*
   was never the shape of that argument. The criterion is: **stop when a
   round's findings are in this document's account of itself, and do not
   stop while a round's findings are in the Controller.** Round 38's were
   in the Controller, so revision 39 is not the last one by fiat either;
   what makes it the last is a round that finds nothing in the design.

   **Acceptance criterion 8 is rescoped here, at its point of definition**
   (revision 49, local round 48's `OPUS-R48-I3`, required acceptance
   criterion 6, superseding every "stands unchanged" restatement below from
   round 46 onward). As stated through revision 48, "0 Blocking and 0
   Important" was read against this document's own account of itself — the
   recogniser-family walk's open column included — which makes the
   criterion's own apparatus, not the Controller design, the thing rounds
   44 through 48 kept failing to clear: `OPUS-R48-B1` reproduces the
   pattern one level up from `OPUS-R46-B1`, and a criterion an apparatus
   that mechanically grows with every revision can perpetually fail is not
   a stopping condition, it is the loop's engine — exactly the argument
   this document already makes for the Controller's own `--max-steps`
   bound (exit code 16, above) and does not, until now, make for itself.
   **From revision 49, acceptance criterion 8 requires a fresh local round
   returning 0 Blocking and 0 Important in the Controller design and in
   the plan's test specifications** — the checkpoints, requirements,
   complexities and test predicates an implementer builds from — **not**
   in this document's account of its own review history. A finding
   confined to a stale figure, a misattributed citation, an unwalked
   recogniser, or any other defect in this document's self-audit apparatus
   is recorded as an open item that does not gate the handoff to the
   manual external stage; a finding that changes what a checkpoint's test
   must assert — `OPUS-R48-B1`'s shape — still gates it, because that is a
   defect in the design being reviewed, not in the review's account of
   itself. Under this wording, rounds 44 through 47 would each have met
   the criterion; round 48 would still, correctly, not, because
   `OPUS-R48-B1` is in the test specification.

   **The reading round 49 applied, recorded here at the criterion's own
   point of definition rather than left to be re-derived** (revision 50,
   local round 49's required acceptance criterion 8): a defect that *lives*
   in the self-audit apparatus — the category-(B) criterion's own wording,
   the recogniser-family walk's table — but whose effect *mislicenses a
   checkpoint's test specification* is graded on where it lands, not on
   where it lives. `OPUS-R49-B1`/`B2` are exactly this shape: the defect is
   in the walk's stated rule and in two of its rows, but its effect is that
   CP1, CP3, CP7, CP8, CP9 and CP4B's test specifications would be built,
   or left un-built, on a rule that does not admit the predicates their own
   declared tests contain — which is a defect in the design being reviewed
   under this criterion's own test, not an amnesty for the apparatus that
   carries it.

   **What round 39 is therefore asked for is narrow.** The mechanism —
   `materialise()`, `pin()`, the `-P -B` re-exec, the runtime-root ladder,
   the refusal taxonomy, the CLI surface — is untouched by this revision
   and has been measured intact by rounds 35, 36 and 37; do not audit it a
   fourth time unless something here touched it, and the diff is the
   evidence that nothing did. Check the one thing this revision changed:
   the stage-aware admissibility model in CP4B. Specifically, that its
   hard/advisory split reproduces what the two frozen commands actually do
   rather than what this document says they do — read
   `validate_manual_plan_review_preconditions` and
   `assert_feedback_matches_bundle` directly, both are in the bundle; that
   the missing-`Reviewed base commit:` fixture is genuinely red against
   revision 38's rule and green against this one, since a repair for an
   admission failure that does not itself discriminate is the worst
   outcome of this round; that the local-stage exemption is right rather
   than an inconsistency, given that applying the rule there would convert
   a `BLOCK` gate into a `/review-plan` launch; and that the residual class
   the model cannot see — a hand edit to a protected path with no state
   write — is genuinely left to `StaleReviewContentIdError` rather than
   quietly assumed away.

   **Round 39 answered that ask in full, and its answer is the criterion's
   first clean reading.** It re-derived the clause table against both
   frozen commands and found every hard and advisory mark right; it checked
   the sole-writer construction behind the content-id comparison instead of
   taking it; it confirmed both discriminating fixtures discriminate, in
   opposite directions; and it confirmed the local-stage exemption is right
   for the reason the exemption gives. It found **nothing in the mechanism
   and nothing in the model**. Its two Important findings are figures the
   consistency apparatus publishes, and its Optional is one clause missing
   from a table — so it is the first round since the criterion was written
   whose entire finding set is in this document's account of itself.

   **What that means for revision 40 is a condition, not a declaration.**
   The criterion's own wording is *"what makes it the last is a round that
   finds nothing in the design"*, and round 39 found nothing in the design
   — but it did find two Important defects, and its own acceptance
   criterion 8 requires a fresh local round returning **0 Blocking and 0
   Important** before another manual external review is requested. The two
   are not in tension: the first says the loop has stopped producing design
   findings, the second says a revision is not shippable while its account
   of itself is wrong. So revision 40 is **not** declared the last revision
   by fiat — the same refusal revision 39 made, and for the same reason —
   but it is the first revision the criterion's stopping clause actually
   reaches, and a clean round 40 sends this item to the manual external
   stage on the strength of a design measured intact by rounds 35, 36, 37
   and 39 and a self-account whose figures reproduce.

   **What round 40 is asked for is narrower still.** The mechanism is
   untouched by this revision and the diff is the evidence; do not audit it
   a fifth time. Two things are worth the round's time. First, **re-run the
   four halves rather than reading their figures.** This revision's entire
   subject is figures that did not reproduce, and extraction is the only
   thing that has ever found that defect — reading found it green three
   times. In particular, the command-line half now publishes five figures
   and two arithmetic identities between them, and each of the last two
   rounds found one half of that set stale while the other half was
   correct; a third recurrence would be visible only to a run. Second,
   **check that the Blocking-finding partition is single-valued across the
   whole bundle.** Revision 40 corrected it at two sites, only one of which
   round 39 named, and a partition that is right in a disposition row and
   stale in this challenge question is the same defect round 39 raised,
   one site over. Everything else here was measured intact by round 39 and
   this revision did not touch it.

   **Round 40 answered that ask and returned the narrowest result this loop
   has produced, but not a clean one.** It re-ran the four halves instead of
   reading them, and every figure revision 40 published reproduced: all five
   command-line figures, both identities, all three round-count occurrences,
   all ten exit-code rows, all thirteen complexity occurrences, the
   fifty-nine frozen digests, the byte-identical registry embed, and the
   partition at all three sites. It found **nothing in the design** for the
   third consecutive round and says so explicitly. Both of its findings are
   in material revision 40 itself added: a pin whose declared authority is a
   gitignored file, and a pin whose declared failing fixture a weaker build
   already passes. So the criterion's own clause reads clean again — the
   findings are in this document's account of itself and none is in the
   Controller — while acceptance criterion 8's clause does not, because a
   required suite that cannot run against a correct build is not a finding
   that can be carried into the manual external stage.

   **The distinction round 40 draws is worth keeping, because it says where
   the remaining risk lives.** Rounds 35 to 37 found the halves'
   *predicates* wrong. Rounds 39 and 40 found their *figures and
   instruments* wrong — and in both, the defect was in what that revision
   had just added, never in older material gone stale. Revision 41 is the
   first revision whose entire subject is the shape of two test
   declarations: what each takes as its authority, what notation it reads,
   and which build its declared fixtures actually discriminate. Both are now
   anchored on committed content, both state their recogniser, and both were
   run over this revision's published text before this paragraph was
   written.

   **What round 41 is asked for is narrower again.** The mechanism is
   untouched for the third consecutive revision and the diff is the
   evidence; do not audit it a sixth time, and CP4B's model, table and
   fixtures are byte-unchanged from what rounds 39 and 40 verified. Three
   things are worth the round's time. First, **run the two rebuilt pins
   rather than reading them**, and for each ask which build its declared
   failing instantiation actually discriminates — that is the exact question
   round 40 asked, and both pins failed it. Second, **check that the
   partition pin's authority is reachable**: every clause it states must be
   decidable from files a clean checkout carries, and the occurrences it
   compares must be findable by the recogniser it declares rather than by a
   reader who knows where they are. Third, **re-run the four halves**, since
   this revision changed the notation one of them publishes its figures in,
   which is precisely the edit that has twice left a figure correct and its
   recogniser stale.

   **Round 41 answered all three, and the answer is the most useful result
   this loop has produced since round 38.** It ran both pins rather than
   reading them, and reported both as discriminating the builds they were
   declared for; it answered the reachability question `yes`, clause by
   clause; and it re-ran all four halves after the revision's last edit and
   reproduced every figure the bundle published, including the alternative
   flag reading. It found **nothing in the design** for the fourth
   consecutive round. And then it found the thing the whole apparatus was
   built to make findable and could not see: **the pin was green and the
